28 The diagram shows a sketch of a wave pattern over a short period of time.
1.0 m
Which description of this wave is correct?
A
The wave is longitudinal, has a wavelength of 20 cm and is stationary.
B
The wave is transverse, has a wavelength of 20 cm and is stationary.
C
The wave is transverse, has a wavelength of 40 cm and is progressive.
D
The wave is transverse, has a wavelength of 40 cm and is stationary.

hints: Notice the many overlapping lines form an envelope with points of zero displacement that stay in the same place - the nodes.
Recall that for a stationary wave the distance from one node to the next node is $\lambda/2$, not $\lambda$.
Count how many node-to-node loops fit in the marked $1.0\text{ m}$ and use $n(\lambda/2)=1.0\text{ m}$ to find $\lambda$ in $\text{cm}$.
walkthrough: Look at the diagram: the vibration is drawn up and down across the centre line, so the displacement is perpendicular to the wave direction. This is a transverse wave.

The sketch over a short period of time shows several positions at once. They all cross at fixed points - nodes - while the amplitude between them grows and shrinks. Fixed nodes mean it is a stationary wave, not a progressive wave.
For a stationary wave, one loop from node to node is half a wavelength: $L_{loop} = \lambda/2$.
Count the loops in the $1.0\text{ m}$ section. There are $5$ complete loops between the two dashed nodes, so $5 \times \lambda/2 = 1.0\text{ m}$.
Rearrange: $\lambda = 2 \times 1.0\text{ m} / 5 = 0.40\text{ m} = 40\text{ cm}$. Unit check confirms $\text{m}$ to $\text{cm}$ conversion.
Transverse plus $40\text{ cm}$ plus stationary matches the description. This is option D.

A.explanation: The pattern shows sideways displacement, not compressions and rarefactions, so it is not longitudinal.

B.explanation: The wave is transverse and stationary, but $20\text{ cm}$ counts one node-to-node loop as a full wavelength instead of half a wavelength.

C.explanation: The wavelength of $40\text{ cm}$ is correct, but the fixed nodes and overlapping traces show a stationary wave, not a progressive wave.

D.explanation: The displacement is transverse, the fixed nodes show it is stationary, and $5$ loops in $1.0\text{ m}$ give $\lambda = 40\text{ cm}$.
